{{short description|American mathematician}}
'''Martin George Scharlemann''' (born 6 December 1948) is an American [[Topology|topologist]] who is a professor at the [[University of California, Santa Barbara]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.math.ucsb.edu/~mgscharl/concise.html|title=Curriculum Vitae – Martin Scharlemann|publisher=}}</ref> He obtained his [[Ph.D.]] from the [[University of California, Berkeley]] under the guidance of [[Robion Kirby]] in 1974.<ref name="MGP">{{cite web|url=http://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=16934|title=The Mathematics Genealogy Project – Martin Scharlemann|publisher=}}</ref>

A conference in his honor was held in 2009 at the [[University of California, Davis]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://users.math.yale.edu/~jj327/conference/|title=Geometric Topology in Dimensions 3 and 4|publisher=}}</ref> He is a Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]], for his "contributions to low-dimensional topology and knot theory."<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://www.ams.org/profession/ams-fellows/fellows2014.pdf|journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society|title=2014 Class of the Fellows of the AMS|volume=61|issue=4|pages=420–421|date=April 2014}}</ref>

[[Abigail Thompson]] was a student of his.<ref name="MGP" /> Together they solved the [[graph planarity]] problem:  There is
an algorithm to decide whether a finite graph in 3-space can be moved in 3-space into a plane.<ref>{{Cite journal|author1-last=Scharlemann|author1-first=Martin|author2-last=Thompson|author2-first=Abigail|year=1991|title=Detecting unknotted graphs in 3-space|journal=Journal of Differential Geometry|language=en|volume=34|issue=2|pages=539–560|doi=10.4310/jdg/1214447220|doi-access=free}}</ref>

He gave the first [[Mathematical proof|proof]] of the classical theorem that [[Knot (mathematics)|knot]]s with [[unknotting number]] one are [[Prime knot|prime]]. He used hard combinatorial arguments for this. Simpler proofs are now known.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Lackenby|first=Marc|date=1997-08-01|title=Surfaces, surgery and unknotting operations|journal=[[Mathematische Annalen]]|language=en|volume=308|issue=4|pages=615–632|doi=10.1007/s002080050093|s2cid=121512073|issn=0025-5831}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Zhang|first=Xingru|date=1991-01-01|title=Unknotting Number One Knots are Prime: A New Proof|jstor=2048550|journal=[[Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society]]|volume=113|issue=2|pages=611–612|doi=10.2307/2048550|doi-access=free}}</ref>

==Selected publications==
{{div col|colwidth=56em|small=yes}}
*"Producing reducible 3-manifolds by surgery on a knot" ''[[Topology (journal)|Topology]]'' '''29''' (1990), no. 4, 481–500. 
*with [[Abigail Thompson]], "Heegaard splittings of (surface) x I are standard" ''[[Mathematische Annalen]]'' '''295''' (1993), no. 3, 549–564. 
*"Sutured manifolds and generalized Thurston norms", ''[[Journal of Differential Geometry]]'' '''29''' (1989), no. 3, 557–614. 
*with [[J. Hyam Rubinstein]], "Comparing Heegaard splittings of non-Haken 3-manifolds" ''Topology''  '''35''' (1996), no. 4, 1005–1026
*"Unknotting number one knots are prime", ''[[Inventiones mathematicae]]'' '''82''' (1985), no. 1, 37–55. 
*with Maggy Tomova,  "Alternate Heegaard genus bounds distance" ''[[Geometry & Topology]]'' '''10''' (2006), 593–617. 
*"Local detection of strongly irreducible Heegaard splittings" ''[[Topology and its Applications]]'', 1998
*with Abigail Thompson – "Link genus and the Conway moves" ''[[Commentarii Mathematici Helvetici]]'', 1989
*"Smooth spheres in <math>\mathbb{R}^4</math> with four critical points are standard" ''[[Inventiones mathematicae]]'', 1985
*"Tunnel number one knots satisfy the Poenaru conjecture" ''[[Topology and its Applications]]'', 1984
*with A Thompson – "Detecting unknotted graphs in 3-space" ''[[Journal of Differential Geometry]]'', 1991
*with A Thompson – "Thin position and Heegaard splittings of the 3-sphere" ''J. Differential Geom'', 1994
{{div col end}}
